test_title: PYST 25: SSC MTS 2023 - General Knowledge (Held On: 14 Sept, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following fundamental duties was added to the Indian Constitution by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002?

options.text: To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem
To protect and to improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures
To provide opportunities for education to his/her child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years
To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom

solution:
The correct answer is __**To provide opportunities for education to his/her child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**, added the fundamental duty of providing opportunities for education to children between the ages of six and fourteen years.
 
• This amendment also led to the insertion of **Article 21A **in the Constitution, making education a fundamental right for children in this age group.
 
• The amendment emphasizes the role of parents and guardians in ensuring that children receive the necessary education.
 
• This duty reflects the importance placed on education as a means of individual and societal development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** fundamental duties** are enshrined in** Part IV-A **of the Constitution of India, under Article 51A.
 
• Originally, ten fundamental duties were listed, but the 86th Amendment Act added an eleventh duty.
 
• The concept of fundamental duties was borrowed from the Constitution of the former Soviet Union and was added to the Indian Constitution by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**.
 
• These duties serve as a constant reminder to citizens to respect the ideals and institutions of the nation.
 
• While these duties are non-justiciable, they are considered essential for the overall development and unity of the country.
